; reuse by the current routine, not persistent game-state identities.
; Puzzle state and 32-entry parallel entity fields. Direction values are

; Audio state: ten parallel voices; effect slots 0..4, music slots 5..9.
; Password scratch aliases share zero page with other bank-local operations.
; NES hardware registers; $4017 is frame control on write and controller 2 on read.

; One count byte followed by count records of signed Y offset, tile, OAM attributes and signed X
; offset. The simple-frame renderer consumes exactly four bytes per sprite; offsets are relative to
; the actor origin. This field is sprite metadata, separate from CHR pixels.
; Six little-endian pointers to the overlay actor's counted simple sprite frames, with effective banks
; 0/1. Each target begins with its own sprite count.

; Silences DMC DAC, enables four tonal/noise channels, invalidates register shadows and clears both playback groups. The following request wrapper saves X/Y; negative requests clear effects, nonnegative requests select an effect.
; Rejects a request masked by an active higher-priority voice. Uses request mask/priority and a pointer table, then allocates inactive voices among slots 4..0 from a counted stream header.
; Preserves allocation flags while installing the request priority and channel mask. Zero remaining voices finishes allocation.
; Continues searching backward through the five effect voices.
; ORs the five voice masks into the active effect-channel mask. The following clear entry stops effects, clears masks/priorities and copies the sixteen-byte default register image.
; Sixteen-byte register shadow reset image copied by the music/effect reset loops. Values
; silence/reset each tracked register before playback resumes.
; Starts a voice with transpose/base-note value $27; falls through into common stream initialization.

; Clears gate scaling, volume, envelope selection and timing adjustment. Reads stream pointer and hardware-register offset from three bytes after the counted header; starts the voice and decrements remaining count.
; Preserves request A, clears the five music slots and resets their register image. Negative A stops here; nonnegative A selects a counted stream list.
; Resolves a music request through a little-endian pointer table and fills inactive slots 9..5 using the common voice initializer.
; The initializer leaves zero when the stream header count is exhausted.
; Searches the remaining music slots down to slot 5.

; Returns from music selection, with a separate update entry immediately afterward. Update disables APU frame IRQs, advances ten voice timers, parses due note/envelope streams, clears inactive effect priorities, then selects effects or music for each hardware channel.
; Uses effect registers when the corresponding active-channel bit is set.
; Writes only changed pulse-one registers, preserving channel-selection carry across the four-byte loop; then selects the pulse-two source.
; Selects the effect pulse-two register image.
; Commits changed pulse-two registers and selects the triangle source.
; Selects the effect triangle register image.
; Commits changed triangle registers and selects the noise source.
; Selects the effect noise register image.
; Commits changed noise registers. If DMC is inactive, restores DAC level $7F; otherwise leaves playback alone.
; Adjacent sign-test masks used by the signed four/five-bit audio getters. These are data operands of

; Advances to the next stream byte. High-three-bit $E0 values dispatch commands; ordinary notes use signed five-bit pitch plus transpose, with channel offset $0C selecting the noise-register path (some command forms also control DMC). A rest reuses duration logic without a new pitch.
; Decodes the rest duration through the shared duration reader.
; Saves decoded duration and normalizes an already active gate counter to one.
; A zero duration immediately parses another event; nonzero duration consumes the next stream byte and returns.
; Re-enters the note parser without waiting for another tick.

; Decodes duration; optionally multiplies it by gate scale using repeated addition and keeps the high byte. Initializes an envelope from a four-byte pointer record. The duration reader recognizes explicit and indexed durations; command dispatch below handles packed volume and saturated signed volume changes.
; Unsigned carry on a positive volume adjustment saturates to fifteen.
; A negative adjustment without carry saturates to zero.
; Supplies zero to the common volume setter.
; Stores the packed-volume result. Command $F2 sets duration-table base to six times its argument; $F3 supplies a direct tick duration.
; Sets tick countdown, disables the gate counter with $FF and advances past the argument.
; Command $F4 sets the gate multiplier. The next comparison recognizes transpose command $F5.
; Stores transpose and resumes note-command parsing.
; Command $F6 selects an envelope. Nonnegative selection initializes it immediately; negative selection retains the disabled marker.
; Calls the common envelope initializer for a nonnegative selection.
; Resumes note parsing, or recognizes pitch-table selector command $F7.
; Stores pitch-table selection and resumes parsing.
; Command $E0 consumes DMC start-address and length register bytes. Command $E2 begins a hardware-register adjustment.
; Reads the first argument for command $E2.

; Preserves the first argument and combines a low nibble from the second with the toggled register-shadow bit before writing through the selected register-image pointer. The following unclassified bytes remain outside this explanation.
; Pops the saved loop byte into the stream destination, advances the decoder and resumes audio
; command dispatch. The caller supplies the stacked byte and destination pointer.
; Recognizes command $E3 for a signed pitch/register adjustment.
; Consumes the adjustment byte; its sign chooses the high-byte extension.
; Uses Y as the sign extension and calls the sixteen-bit register adder. The bounded voice-register writer returns to the now-classified parser continuation.
; Resume note-command decoding after the bounded voice register writer returns.
; Recognizes command $E1, which sets an audio control byte whose wider consumer is unresolved.
; Stores the control byte and resumes parsing.
; Clears the note countdown before common envelope shutdown.
; Clears the envelope countdown, recomputes volume through the shared setter and returns.
; Loads and saves the voice-local software-stack cursor around stream control. The flow interpreter handles $F8 absolute jump and dispatches the remaining call/loop commands.
; Begins reading the two-byte target for $FA stream call.
; Reads a little-endian stream target, pushes the current stream position onto the per-voice software stack, then installs the target. This stack is RAM, separate from the CPU return stack.
; Restores stream pointer from the software stack and advances its cursor by two.
; Command $FC pushes the loop count and current stream pointer. Command $FD decrements that count, restores the saved pointer until zero, then discards the three-byte loop record and advances.
; Recognizes $FE; consumes one byte before the final advance.
; Consumes the second byte for the recognized skip form.
; Returns for unhandled flow command values.
; Increments the sixteen-bit stream pointer and reads the byte at its new position with the caller-supplied Y offset.
; Carries low-byte wrap into the stream-pointer high byte.
; Returns the pointed byte. A separate pitch entry follows: resolves a selected period table, indexes it by twice the note, writes timer bytes and merges the channel trigger/shadow flags.
; Ten trigger masks: five music voices use zero and five effect voices use $20. The pitch writer
; combines this with channel ownership before writing APU state.

; Gate countdown starts the envelope release pointer when it expires; zero/$FF gates are inactive. Envelope parsing advances its stream, recognizes delay bytes and dispatches signed pitch, volume, duty and flow commands.
; Extracts a signed low-nibble delta for the pitch adjustment.
; Adds the decoded signed delta to the timer-register pair.
; Bit $10 decides whether the event uses a one-tick delay or immediately parses another envelope byte.
; Advances the current stream pointer after an envelope operation.
; High-three-bit $40 sets volume directly; $60 adds a signed low-nibble delta to the current low-nibble volume before clamping.
; Supplies the upper bound of fifteen.
; Applies volume through the shared mixer, or writes duty bits while preserving the low six register bits. Extended commands include a raw second-register write.
; Reads the raw register argument for extended command $F0.
; Writes the channel register at base offset plus one; the bounded register-write continuation resumes the envelope parser.
; Resume envelope-command decoding after the bounded voice register writer returns.
; Command $FF stops the envelope. Other extended commands reuse the common software-stack flow interpreter, saving its cursor separately from the note stream.
; Returns for an unrecognized envelope command class.

; Combines the requested low-nibble volume with the stored high-nibble attenuation, clamps, then applies group attenuation (effects 0..4, music 5..9). Triangle becomes on/off at threshold four; other channels preserve duty and force constant-volume bits.
; Clamps the attenuated output volume to zero.
; Writes the mixed volume or triangle gate. A separate helper extracts and sign-extends a four-bit stream delta into A/Y.
; Read the current stream byte as signed five-bit A, with Y holding its sign extension (0 or FF). Bit
; 4 selects sign extension; this getter does not advance the stream.
; The positive five-bit field already has Y=0.
; Adds A plus sign-extension Y to the low/high timer-register image for the current channel.
; Big-endian APU timer periods, descending from 2047 to 28. The pitch reader selects two-byte
; entries; the original tuning/rounding rule is unresolved.
